lessons.title: Pet Care and Dog Walking Errands
lessons.body: Pet care errands include dog walking, feeding, grooming runs, and vet visits. In many African cities, busy professionals own dogs but lack time for midday walks. Charge per walk: in Nairobi, KES 500â800 for a 30-minute walk; in Lagos, NGN 3,000â5,000. For feeding visits, charge KES 1,000 per visit. Always carry a leash, waste bags, and fresh water. Build a route with 3â4 dogs in the same neighborhood to maximize earnings. For vet errands, confirm appointment times, transport the pet safely in a crate or with a pet taxi, and keep a record of vaccinations. Use WhatsApp to send photo updates to owners after each walk. Insurance is rare, so create a simple liability waiver. Start by offering free trial walks to friends' pets to get testimonials. Then advertise on local Facebook groups, vet clinics, and apartment notice boards. Key safety: never walk more than two dogs at once unless trained; avoid hot pavement during midday; and learn basic first aid for pets. For overnight pet sitting, charge a daily rate (KES 2,500â4,000). Keep a pet first-aid kit with bandages, antiseptic, and tick remover. In Africa, be aware of ticks and snakes in some areas. Always ask owners about allergies, medications, and emergency vet contacts. Reliable pet care builds loyal clients who travel frequently, giving you recurring income.

lessons.title: Elderly Care Errands and Companion Services
lessons.body: Elderly care errands involve grocery shopping, pharmacy pickups, bill payments, and accompanying seniors to medical appointments. In many African communities, extended family may live far away, so paid companions fill a gap. Charge hourly: KES 400â600 in Kenya, NGN 2,500â4,000 in Nigeria. Services include reading mail, writing letters, and helping with mobile banking. For medical visits, arrive 30 minutes early, bring a list of medications, and take notes for family. Build trust by being punctual, patient, and respectful. Learn basic signs of stroke, dehydration, and low blood sugar. Keep an emergency contact card. For companionship, play cards, take walks, or assist with video calls to relatives. Always get permission before moving furniture or handling finances. A simple contract outlining tasks, hours, and payment terms is essential. Advertise through churches, mosques, community centers, and retirement homes. Many clients prefer a weekly schedule: e.g., Monday and Thursday, 9amâ1pm. Use a notebook to log each visit: what was done, what was purchased, and any concerns. Payment can be cash or mobile money (M-Pesa, Airtel Money). Avoid handling large sumsâuse receipts. For grocery runs, ask for a list and a budget cap. In some cultures, it's polite to remove shoes and accept a cup of tea. Build a reputation for honesty and kindness; word-of-mouth referrals are powerful. Consider taking a short first-aid course. This service is rewarding and in high demand as populations age.

lessons.title: Child-Related Errands: School Pickups, Activities
lessons.body: Child-related errands include school pickups, dropping kids at music lessons or sports, buying school supplies, and waiting during extracurriculars. Parents pay well for reliability. In South Africa, charge R80âR150 per trip; in Kenya, KES 500â800. You must be vetted: provide a police clearance certificate (costs about KES 1,000 in Kenya, R150 in South Africa). Always carry your ID and a letter from the parent. For school pickup, arrive 15 minutes early, park legally, and wait at the designated gate. Confirm the child's full name, class, and teacher. Never let a child go with anyone else without written permission. For activities, keep a schedule with times, addresses, and instructor contacts. Use a checklist: water bottle, snack, sports kit, homework folder. After pickup, send a WhatsApp message to the parent: 'Picked up Aisha at 3:15pm, heading to ballet.' For supply runs, use a shopping list app like Google Keep. Buy exact itemsâbrands matter. Keep receipts. For waiting during lessons, use the time to run nearby errands or read. Charge extra for waiting beyond 30 minutes. Safety: never leave a child unattended in a car; use child locks; and avoid discussing family matters with strangers. Build a portfolio of 3â5 families for steady weekday income. Advertise at school gates (with permission), parenting groups on Facebook, and local libraries. In some areas, you may need a background check from a recognized agency. Always have a backup plan if a child is sick or school closes early. This service requires patience, punctuality, and a genuine love for children.

lessons.title: Corporate Errand Services for Businesses
lessons.body: Corporate errands serve small and medium businesses: bank deposits, document delivery, office supply restocking, lunch runs, and queue-standing at government offices. Charge per errand or a monthly retainer. In Lagos, a bank deposit run costs NGN 5,000â10,000; a monthly retainer for 2 hours daily is NGN 80,000â150,000. In Nairobi, similar services range KES 1,500â3,000 per errand. You need a professional look: clean shirt, closed shoes, and a folder for documents. Always get a signed receipt for documents delivered. For bank deposits, count cash twice, use a deposit slip, and get a stamped acknowledgment. For government queues (e.g., KRA, NHIF, licensing), arrive by 6am, carry a book and power bank, and update the client via WhatsApp every hour. For office supplies, use a shared spreadsheet to track inventory and reorder points. For lunch runs, collect orders by 10am, use a food delivery app or call ahead, and deliver by 12:30pm. Keep a cooler bag for hot food. Invoicing: use a simple template with your business name, date, description, and amount. Payment via bank transfer or mobile money. Build relationships with receptionists and security guardsâthey can speed up access. Never sign for anything you don't understand. For confidential documents, use a sealed envelope and hand-deliver only to the named recipient. Consider a non-disclosure agreement for sensitive work. Advertise by visiting offices with a one-page flyer listing services and rates. Offer a free trial errand for the first client. Reliability and discretion are your selling points. Many corporates prefer a single trusted runner over multiple gig workers.

lessons.title: Concierge Services for Hotels and Events
lessons.body: Concierge errands for hotels and events include airport pickups, restaurant reservations, ticket purchases, gift shopping, and last-minute supplies. Hotels often outsource to freelance concierges. Charge per task: airport pickup $20â$50 in major cities; restaurant booking $10; gift shopping $15 plus cost. For events, you might handle guest check-in, luggage storage, or vendor runs. Build a contact list of reliable taxi drivers, florists, and caterers. For airport pickups, track flight numbers, arrive 30 minutes early, and hold a sign with the guest's name. Use a car with working AC and a phone charger. For restaurant reservations, call ahead, confirm dietary needs, and send confirmation to the guest. For gift shopping, ask for budget and preferences, send photos of options, and get approval before buying. Keep receipts and a small float for emergencies. In hotels, dress smartly (black trousers, white shirt) and never enter guest rooms without permission. For events, create a checklist: name tags, pens, water, extension cords, and backup power. Charge an hourly rate for event days (KES 500â1,000 per hour). Use a WhatsApp group with the event planner for real-time updates. Payment: 50% deposit, 50% on completion. Advertise by dropping business cards at hotel front desks, event venues, and wedding planners. Offer a 10% commission for referrals. Important: never share guest information. Sign a confidentiality agreement. For hotel concierge, learn basic local attractions and transport options. This niche pays well if you are polished, discreet, and fast. Start with small guesthouses and build up to 5-star hotels.

lessons.title: Seasonal and Holiday Errand Planning
lessons.body: Seasonal and holiday errands spike during Christmas, Ramadan, Easter, and school holidays. Plan ahead to maximize income. In December, demand for gift shopping, party supplies, and airport runs doubles. Charge 20â30% more during peak weeks. For Ramadan, errands include food deliveries at sunset, prayer mat purchases, and charity distributions. For Easter, focus on church events and family gatherings. For school holidays, offer childcare errands and activity drop-offs. Create a holiday calendar: list key dates (e.g., Dec 15âJan 5, Ramadan dates, Easter week). Two weeks before, send a WhatsApp broadcast to past clients: 'Booking now for holiday errandsâlimited slots.' Offer packages: e.g., 'Christmas Shopping Package: 5 errands for KES 5,000.' For gift shopping, use a shared spreadsheet with names, budgets, and ideas. Buy in bulk from markets (e.g., Gikomba in Nairobi, Balogun in Lagos) for better prices. For food deliveries, partner with a caterer or restaurant. For airport runs, book a reliable driver in advance. Keep a cooler and thermal bags for perishables. For charity distributions, coordinate with local NGOs and get receipts. Safety: avoid carrying large cash; use mobile money. Keep a backup of your phone. During holidays, traffic is heavyâadd 30 minutes to travel time. Charge a surcharge for late-night errands. After the season, send thank-you notes and ask for testimonials. Save 30% of peak earnings for the slow months (JanuaryâFebruary). Advertise on community WhatsApp groups and church bulletins. This planning turns seasonal chaos into reliable profit.
